create.title: Exact finite reflected vector Hankel kernel
create.statement_tex: On finite u,v,w rectangles with positive outside abscissae, shift the radial w-segment from Re w=c to lambda=1-c', choose c'>1+(a+b)/2 and S>(U+V)/2, retain both radial horizontal sides, and set s=1-w. Expanding F_(-(u+v))(s) absolutely yields the exact dual-index kernel 1_(hq=m)chi_4(q) times the triple integral of A_j(u,v)(h/q)^((u+v)/2)G_v(1-s)K_(u+v)(1-s)m^(-s), where K_z(1-s)=2^(2s+z-1)pi^(1-2s)Gamma((s-z/2)/2)Gamma((1+s+z/2)/2)/[Gamma((1-s+z/2)/2)Gamma((2-s-z/2)/2)]. The crossed arithmetic residue is A_j G_v(1-z/2)L(1-z,chi_4). Height, hard-Perron, corner, radial-endpoint, and all horizontal-side terms remain explicit when their contours are moved. No infinite-height limit is asserted.
create.next_action: Use the finite kernel as the sole reflected operator definition; choose and validate a nested contour-height exhaustion before taking limits.

create.title: Archimedean conductor and transition diagram for the vector kernel
create.statement_tex: For s=sigma+it and z=zeta+i eta, the completed degree-two conductor is 4(1+|t+eta/2|)(1+|t-eta/2|). For bounded eta and a smooth radial shell x asymp N, the complete Hankel inversion has phases e(plus or minus sqrt(mx)); the stationary branch against e(sqrt(Xx)) localizes to |m-X|<<sqrt(X/N), the accepted near-product return. For unbounded eta, separate: outer Stirling where both |t plus or minus eta/2| are large; single-transition strips where one is O(1); and double-bounded range, possible only for bounded eta. Since eta=Im u+Im v, the single-transition strips sweep the hard-Perron height. No estimate for these strips or horizontal sides is asserted.
create.next_action: Change to diagonal heights alpha=t+eta/2 and beta=t-eta/2; derive each single-transition kernel without extrapolating fixed-order Stirling.

create.title: Swept single-transition and horizontal-side vector operator
create.statement_tex: For the exact finite vector Hankel identity, control the portions |Im s-Im(u+v)/2|<<1 and |Im s+Im(u+v)/2|<<1, together with all radial horizontal sides under a specified nested exhaustion S=S(U,V) that dominates U+V, every crossed arithmetic/axial residue, and the hard symmetric u-Perron limit. A target-sized estimate must be uniform in the remaining large gamma height and actual scale/floor/profile variables. Bounded-shift Hankel formulas do not imply it.
create.next_action: Use diagonal gamma-height coordinates and test nested contour exhaustion plus exact single-transition gamma kernels.

create.title: Fixed-order Voronoi sources do not control the swept vector transition
create.statement_tex: The audited Banerjee-Khurana formulas are fixed-order odd-character identities for analytic finite-interval weights and do not supply uniform large-imaginary-order estimates or accept the hard top jump. The audited Kiral-Zhou architecture does not directly specialize to the ramified polar degree-two product with three contour heights, finite horizontal sides, and a maximal Perron limit. Neither source proves the swept transition/horizontal operator estimate.
create.next_action: Do not cite fixed-order formulas for a uniform transition estimate; derive the transition kernel first, then search for an exact matching theorem.

update.statement_tex: For the exact finite vector kernel M9-M1-finite-vector-Hankel-identity, prove a target-sized signed operator estimate after every arithmetic, height, hard-Perron, corner, and radial-endpoint residue is separately controlled and after radial/outside horizontal sides are removed by a validated nested exhaustion. The bounded-shift region returns to the near-product problem; the smallest unresolved component is M9-M1-swept-transition-horizontal-operator.
update.next_action: Attack the diagonal-height single-transition strips and nested horizontal-side exhaustion; do not replace them by bounded-shift Hankel waves.
Use the exact finite vector identity; the swept transition/horizontal operator is now the principal reflected-mode blocker.

reject.reason: Their gamma decay is not uniform when the radial height approaches either swept transition plane, and no nested exhaustion has been proved.
For large Im z, one gamma argument becomes bounded on t=plus or minus Im z/2; fixed-order two-factor Stirling is invalid there.
The bounded-shift stationary phase localizes to m near X, exactly the previously accepted near-product return map.
The audited sources do not provide a uniform large-imaginary-order, hard-jump, three-height estimate with finite horizontal sides.

No target-sized vector estimate was proved.
Finite operator infrastructure does not prove the target.
